100862.q: When is the number 112 especially useful?
100862.e: Abroad, you often do not know the emergency numbers. 112 is the same in many European countries.
100862.m: On holiday in Europe, I dial 112 in an emergency.

100863.q: How many digits does the European emergency number have?
100863.e: The European emergency number is 112, so one, one, two. That is three digits.
100863.m: The European emergency number has only three digits.

100864.q: Which emergency number is used mainly in the USA?
100864.e: In the USA and Canada, people dial 911. In Europe, it is 112.
100864.m: In Europe I dial 112, and in the USA 911.

100865.q: Who do you reach in Switzerland when you dial 112?
100865.e: If you dial 112, you get through to an emergency control centre. They send the right help.
100865.m: With 112, I reach an emergency control centre.

100866.q: What can you dial the European emergency number 112 for?
100866.e: On 112, they help you with accidents, fire or danger. It does not matter what kind of emergency it is.

100867.q: Can you call 112 with a mobile phone too?
100867.e: 112 works with mobiles and landlines. That is why you can also dial it when you are out and about.
100867.m: I can dial 112 on a mobile phone too.

100868.q: What do you do first with a small graze?
a: Not look at it at all
100868.e: First you wash dirt out of the wound with clean water. Then a plaster goes on.

100869.q: Which part of a plaster should you not touch with your fingers?
a: The soft pad in the middle
The sticky strips on the outside
100869.e: The pad lies directly on the wound. It should stay clean so that no germs get in.
100869.m: I do not touch the pad of a plaster.

100870.q: What is a plaster on a small wound for?
100870.e: The plaster covers the wound. That way less dirt and fewer germs get in.
100870.m: A plaster protects a wound from dirt.

100871.q: Where should plasters be kept at home?
100871.e: In the first aid kit, everything for first aid is in one place. That way you can find it quickly.
100871.m: I keep plasters in the first aid kit.

100872.q: When do you put a new plaster on a wound?
a: When the old one is wet or dirty
When the old one is still completely clean
100872.e: A wet or dirty plaster no longer protects well. Then you put on a new clean plaster.
100872.m: I replace a dirty plaster with a new one.

100873.q: When is a plaster NOT enough any more?
a: When a wound is bleeding heavily
100873.e: For heavy bleeding, you need a bandage and help from adults. A plaster is only for small wounds.
100873.m: If there is heavy bleeding, I get help straight away.

100874.q: What do you do before you put a plaster on someone?
100874.e: Clean hands carry fewer germs to the wound. That is why you wash them first.
100874.m: Before treating a wound, I wash my hands.

100875.q: What can you use to treat a clean wound against germs before putting on a plaster?
100875.e: A disinfectant from the first aid kit kills germs. Then you put the plaster on.
100875.m: Disinfectant kills germs in a wound.

100876.q: What is the wound called when you fall on your knee and scrape the skin?
100876.e: With a graze, the top layer of skin has been rubbed off. It usually only bleeds a little.
100876.m: Scraped skin is called a graze.

100877.q: What is a roll of bandage usually made of?
100877.e: A bandage is made of fabric such as gauze or stretchy material. You can wrap it around a wound.
100877.m: A bandage is made of soft fabric.

100878.q: How tight should a bandage be?
100878.e: A bandage that is too tight cuts off the blood. A bandage that is too loose slips off.
100878.m: A bandage sits firmly, but not too tightly.

100879.q: How can you tell that a bandage on an arm is too tight?
a: The fingers turn blue and cold
The fingers turn warm and pink
100879.e: If too little blood reaches the fingers, they turn blue, cold or tingle. Then the bandage must be loosened.
100879.m: Blue, cold fingers show that a bandage is too tight.

100880.q: What is the cloth called that you can use to support an injured arm?
100880.e: With a triangular bandage, you can make an arm sling. That keeps the injured arm still.
100880.m: I support an arm with a triangular bandage.

100881.q: What do you do first if a wound is bleeding heavily?
a: Press firmly on the wound and get help
Rinse the wound with water and wait
Let the wound dry in the air
Stick a small plaster next to it
100881.e: Pressure on the wound slows the bleeding. At the same time, you get help or call the emergency number 144.
100881.m: With heavy bleeding, press firmly on the wound.

100882.q: Where in Switzerland can you often find a first aid kit?
100882.e: Many cars, schools and sports halls have a first aid kit. It contains bandages and plasters.
100882.m: Schools and cars have first aid kits.

100883.q: Why do you need disposable gloves when putting on a bandage?
a: To protect against blood and germs
100883.e: Gloves protect both helpers and injured people from germs. You find them in the first aid kit.
100883.m: I put on gloves when bandaging.

100884.q: What do you put directly on a wound first, before wrapping it?
100884.e: A sterile dressing lies cleanly on the wound. You wrap the bandage over it.
100884.m: A clean dressing goes on the wound first.

100885.q: What helps straight after spraining your foot?
100885.e: Cooling and raising it make the swelling less bad. Afterwards an adult should check whether you need to see a doctor.
100885.m: I cool a sprained foot and raise it.

100886.q: Why do you never put ice directly on the skin?
100886.e: Ice directly on the skin can cause cold damage. That is why you always wrap it in a cloth.
100886.m: I always wrap ice in a cloth.

100887.q: What do you wrap an ice pack in before putting it on the skin?
100887.e: A thin cloth protects the skin from too much cold. The ice pack still cools well.
100887.m: I only put an ice pack on the skin with a cloth.

100888.q: What can you cool with if there is no ice pack?
100888.e: A cloth with cold water also cools. You make it wet again when it gets warm.
100888.m: A wet, cold cloth also cools well.

100889.q: What does cooling often help with?
100889.e: Cooling helps a bump to swell less. If there is a bad headache or vomiting, you must go to the doctor.

100890.q: What happens when you cool a bruise?
100890.e: Cold makes the blood vessels narrower. Less blood leaks out, so the area swells less.

100891.q: What do you cool a small burn with?
100891.e: Cool but not ice-cold water eases the pain. Ice cubes directly on the skin can do harm.
100891.m: I cool a small burn with water.

100892.q: What do you take out of the freezer when you need to cool something quickly?
100892.e: An ice pack is ready in the freezer. You put it, protected, on the injured area.
100892.m: An ice pack from the freezer helps with bumps.

100893.q: Where do ticks wait for people and animals?
100893.e: Ticks sit on grasses and shrubs. They get brushed off onto you as you walk past.
100893.m: Ticks wait in grass and bushes.

100894.q: What do you do after a trip to the woods?
100894.e: Ticks are small and often bite in warm places. If you check yourself, you find them early.
100894.m: After the woods, I check my body for ticks.

100895.q: What is the best way to remove a tick?
a: With tick tweezers or ordinary tweezers
100895.e: With tick tweezers or ordinary tweezers, you grip the tick close to the skin. Then you pull it out slowly.
100895.m: I pull a tick out with tweezers.

100896.q: When are ticks mainly active in Switzerland?
100896.e: Ticks are active when it is warm enough. That is usually from spring into autumn.
100896.m: Ticks are active from spring to autumn.

100897.q: How many legs does an adult tick have?
100897.e: Adult ticks have four pairs of legs. That makes eight legs.
100897.m: Like spiders, ticks have eight legs.

100898.q: What is best to wear in the woods to protect against ticks?
100898.e: Long trousers and closed shoes protect the skin. Then it is harder for ticks to reach your legs.
100898.m: In the woods, I wear long trousers.

100899.q: How long should you keep an eye on the spot after a tick bite?
100899.e: Illnesses after a tick bite sometimes only show up later. That is why you check the spot for a few weeks.
100899.m: After a tick bite, I watch the spot for a few weeks.

100900.q: What is a warning sign a few days after a tick bite?
a: A red ring that gets bigger
100900.e: A red ring that grows is called a bull's-eye rash. Then you must see a doctor, because it can be an illness.
100900.m: If a red ring is growing, I go to the doctor.

100901.q: What does a tick feed on?
100901.e: Ticks bite people and animals and suck blood. They become much fatter as they do so.

100902.q: What often stays stuck in the skin after a bee sting?
100902.e: A honeybee's sting has tiny barbs. That is why it often stays in the skin along with the venom sac.
100902.m: After a bee sting, the sting is often stuck in the skin.

100903.q: How do you remove a bee sting?
a: Do not remove it at all
100903.e: The most important thing is to remove the sting quickly. It is best to scrape it off sideways with a fingernail.
100903.m: I remove a bee sting quickly.

100904.e: Bees only sting when they feel that they or their colony are under threat. The sting is how they defend themselves.
100904.m: A bee stings when it defends itself.

100905.q: When is a sting in the mouth dangerous?
100905.e: A sting in the mouth or throat can swell so much that it is hard to breathe. Then you dial 144 at once and let the person suck ice.
100905.m: If someone is stung in the mouth, I call 144 at once.

100906.q: What is important if someone has a bee allergy?
100906.e: With an allergy, the whole body can react, for example with difficulty breathing. Then you call the emergency number 144 at once.
100906.m: With an allergy, I get help immediately.

100907.q: How should you behave when a bee is flying around you?
100907.e: Hectic movements make bees nervous. People who stay calm get stung less often.

100908.q: Why should you not drink from open cans of fizzy drink outdoors?
100908.e: Wasps like sweet things and crawl into cans. A sting in the mouth is dangerous, so it is better to drink from a glass or with a straw.
100908.m: Outdoors, I look into my glass before drinking.

100909.q: Which insect usually loses its sting when it stings?
100909.e: The honeybee's sting has barbs and gets stuck. Wasps can pull their sting back out.
100909.m: Only the honeybee usually loses its sting when it stings.

100910.q: Roughly how long should you cool a small burn?
100910.e: Cooling for this long eases the pain and protects the skin. For large burns, you call for help immediately.
100910.m: I cool a burn with water for several minutes.

100911.q: What does NOT belong on a burn?
100911.e: Butter, flour or toothpaste make the wound dirty. They can cause an infection.

100912.q: What do you do with a burn blister?
100912.e: The blister protects the skin underneath from germs. That is why you do not pop it.
100912.m: I do not pop a burn blister.

100913.q: What can you easily burn yourself on in the kitchen?
100913.e: Hobs, pans and the oven get very hot. That is why care is important in the kitchen.
100913.m: I am very careful near the hot cooker.

100914.q: What do you do if a person's clothes are on fire?
a: Get them to roll on the ground and get help
100914.e: Running fans the fire. Rolling on the ground or using a fire blanket smothers the flames, and you call for help at once.
100914.m: Burning clothes are smothered on the ground.

100915.e: Hot liquids or steam injure the skin. This is called a scald.
100915.m: Hot water can scald your skin.

100916.q: What can you cool when you have sunburn?
100916.e: Sunburn is a mild burn of the skin. Cool compresses help against the burning feeling.
100916.m: I cool sunburn with damp cloths.

100917.q: When must you call the emergency number at once for a burn?
100917.e: Large burns are dangerous, especially for children. Then you call 144 at once.

100918.q: What do you do first as a child when there is an accident?
100918.e: Adults are better able to help and can call the emergency number. That is why you fetch someone at once.
100918.m: If there is an accident, I fetch an adult at once.

100919.q: What do you pay attention to before helping at the scene of an accident?
100919.e: If you put yourself in danger, you cannot help anyone. The road, for example, is dangerous.
100919.m: When helping, I look after myself first.

100920.q: Who can you ask for help in the playground?
100920.e: Teachers are on playground duty and know what to do. They can also call for help.
100920.m: In the playground, I fetch the teacher.

100921.q: What do you do while an adult calls the emergency number?
100921.e: An injured person is often frightened. If someone stays with them and talks to them, it calms them down.
100921.m: I stay with injured people and comfort them.

100922.q: What can you say to an injured person?
100922.e: Calming words make people feel safer. The person then knows that someone will come soon.
100922.m: I calm injured people with kind words.

100923.q: What do you do if there is no adult nearby?
100923.e: Children may and should call the emergency number too. The control centre will tell you exactly what you can do.
100923.m: Even as a child, I may call the emergency number.

100924.q: How do you call loudly for help?
100924.e: Other people hear loud, clear shouting more quickly. Then they come to help.
100924.m: I call for help loudly and clearly.

100925.q: Which address should you know by heart for emergencies?
a: The address of the zoo in Paris
The address of a toy shop
100925.e: When you make an emergency call, you must say where you are. If you know your address, you can quickly get help to your home.
100925.m: I know my address by heart.

100926.q: What do you tell an adult that you fetch to help?
100926.e: The adult must quickly know what is going on and where to go. That way they can help straight away.
100926.m: I say briefly what has happened and where.

100927.q: What is the phone number of Rega?
100927.e: Rega, the Swiss Air Rescue service, can be reached on 1414.

100928.q: How does Rega usually reach injured people?
100928.e: Rega flies rescue helicopters. That way it can quickly reach places in the mountains too.

100929.e: Rega helicopters are red and white. That makes them easy to spot in the sky.
100929.m: Rega helicopters are red and white.

100930.e: Rega rescues people in need with helicopters and air ambulance jets. It has existed since 1952.
100930.m: Rega is the Swiss Air Rescue service.

100932.q: What are the people called who support Rega with a yearly contribution?
100932.e: Rega gets a lot of money from its patrons. That way it can pay for its helicopters.

100933.q: Where does the Rega helicopter help especially often?
100933.e: In the mountains, the journey by car takes a long time. The helicopter is much faster there.
100933.m: Rega often helps in the mountains.

100934.q: Who is on board the helicopter during a Rega mission?
100934.e: The crew includes a pilot, a paramedic and an emergency doctor. That way they can help injured people right on the spot.
100934.m: A doctor flies on the Rega helicopter.

100935.q: What does an ambulance switch on during an emergency journey?
100935.e: Blue lights and the siren warn others. They should clear the way.
100935.m: When I see blue lights and hear a siren, I make way.

100936.q: What do you do on your bike when an ambulance comes with its siren on?
a: Stay in the middle of the road
100936.e: Emergency vehicles need a clear road. Stopping at the side helps them.
100936.m: When an ambulance comes, I make way.

100938.e: Paramedics look after people who are ill or injured. They take them to hospital.

100939.q: Where does the ambulance usually take injured people?
100939.e: In hospital, doctors continue to treat the injured.
100939.m: The ambulance takes injured people to hospital.

100940.q: What is on board an ambulance?
100940.e: An ambulance has bandages, medicines and equipment. With these, the paramedics can help on the way.
100940.m: An ambulance carries equipment to help injured people.

100941.q: Why is the word “AMBULANCE” written back to front on the front of some ambulances?
a: So it can be read in the rear-view mirror
100941.e: A driver sees everything mirrored in the rear-view mirror. That way they read the word the right way round.
100941.m: Mirror writing can be read correctly in a rear-view mirror.

100942.q: May an ambulance with blue lights and siren drive through a red light at a junction?
100942.e: In an emergency, rescue vehicles with blue lights and siren may ignore traffic rules. But they must drive carefully.
100942.m: An ambulance on an emergency may carefully drive through a red light.

100943.q: What does a foil emergency blanket usually look like?
100943.e: An emergency blanket is a thin foil. One side shines gold, the other silver.
100943.m: An emergency blanket shines gold and silver.

100944.q: What is an emergency blanket mainly for?
a: It replaces an umbrella on walks
100944.e: Injured people get cold quickly. The foil keeps warmth near the body and protects against wind and wet.
100944.m: An emergency blanket keeps injured people warm.

100945.q: How thick is an emergency blanket?
100945.e: An emergency blanket is a wafer-thin foil. That is why, folded up, it fits into any small bag.
100945.m: An emergency blanket is as thin as foil.

100946.q: Where can you find an emergency blanket?
100946.e: Emergency blankets belong in first aid kits and hiking first aid packs.
100946.m: There is an emergency blanket in the first aid kit.

100947.q: Why do you pack an emergency blanket for a mountain hike?
a: Because it is light and small
Because it shines like a lamp
100947.e: An emergency blanket weighs almost nothing. In an emergency in the mountains, it protects against cold.
100947.m: An emergency blanket is light and fits into any rucksack.

100948.q: What do you do with an emergency blanket for an injured person?
a: Fan air at them with it
100948.e: You wrap the injured person loosely, leaving the face free. That way they lose less heat.
100948.m: I cover injured people with an emergency blanket.

100949.q: What else does the shiny emergency blanket help with?
a: Rescuers can see it from far away
100949.e: The shiny foil reflects light. That makes it easier to find injured people, for example from a helicopter.
100949.m: The shiny emergency blanket can be seen from far away.

100950.q: What is an emergency blanket made of?
100950.e: It is made of a thin plastic foil with a wafer-thin layer of metal. That is why it shines.
100950.m: An emergency blanket is made of shiny foil.

101608.q: Which parts of the body does a sun hat with a wide brim protect?
101608.e: The wide brim casts shade on the face, ears and neck. The hat itself covers the head.
101608.m: A hat with a wide brim protects your head, face and neck.

101609.q: What is the rim of a hat called?
101609.e: The rim that sticks out from a hat is called the brim. The wider the brim, the more shade it gives.
101609.m: The rim of a hat is called the brim.

101610.q: Which colour of hat gets less hot in the sun?
101610.e: Light colours reflect a lot of sunlight. Dark colours absorb the light and get hot.
101610.m: Light clothes and hats stay cooler in the sun.

101611.q: What does a cap with neck protection have at the back?
a: A piece of fabric over the neck
101611.e: With this cap, a piece of fabric hangs down at the back. It protects the neck from sunburn.
101611.m: Neck protection covers the neck with fabric.

101612.q: Why should small children wear a hat in the sun?
a: Their head is sensitive to the sun
101612.e: Children's scalps are often not well covered by hair, and their skin is sensitive. A hat protects against sunburn and overheating.
101612.m: Children always wear a hat in the sun.

a: A hat made of woven straw
101613.e: Straw hats are woven from dried stalks. They are light and let air through.
101613.m: A straw hat is light and airy.

101614.q: When is a sun hat most important?
a: At midday when it is very sunny
Early in the morning in bed
101614.e: At midday, the sun is highest and strongest. That is when your head needs the most protection.
101614.m: At midday, your head needs the most sun protection.

101615.q: What is the strap under the chin on some sun hats for?
a: So the wind does not blow the hat away
101615.e: The chin strap holds the hat firmly on your head. That way it stays on even in the wind or while you play.
101615.m: A chin strap holds your hat on in the wind.

101616.q: Can we see UV rays with our eyes?
101616.e: UV rays are a part of sunlight that our eyes cannot see. Even so, they affect our skin and eyes.
101616.m: UV rays are invisible, but they still have an effect.

101617.q: Where does most of the UV radiation that reaches us come from?
101617.e: As well as light and warmth, the sun also sends out UV rays. It is our biggest source of UV.
101617.m: Most UV radiation comes from the sun.

101618.q: What can too much UV radiation do to your skin?
a: Cause a gap in your teeth
101618.e: UV rays damage the skin. It turns red, gets hot and hurts.
101618.m: Too much UV radiation causes sunburn.

101619.q: Does UV radiation also get through clouds?
101619.e: Clouds only block part of the UV radiation. That is why you can get sunburnt on cloudy days too.
101619.m: Even when it is cloudy, the sun can burn your skin.

a: In the shade of a house
101620.e: In the mountains, the layer of air above us is thinner. It blocks less UV radiation.
101620.m: The sun is stronger in the mountains than in the valley.

101621.q: Which layer high up in the air blocks a lot of UV radiation?
101621.e: The ozone layer lies high above the Earth. It absorbs a large part of the dangerous UV radiation.
101621.m: The ozone layer protects us from a lot of UV radiation.

101622.q: Why does your skin go brown in summer?
a: It is protecting itself from UV rays
101622.e: In the sun, the skin makes more dark pigment. This protects a little against UV rays, but not enough.
101622.m: Tanned skin is a sign that your skin is defending itself.

101623.q: Apart from the skin, which parts of the body can UV rays also damage?
101623.e: UV rays can irritate the eyes and damage them over time. Good sunglasses help.
101623.m: Your eyes also need protection from UV rays.

a: A lot of sun on your head and neck
101624.e: If the sun shines for a long time on an unprotected head and neck, the brain gets irritated. This is called sunstroke.
101624.m: Sunstroke comes from too much sun on your head.

101625.q: What is a typical sign of sunstroke?
101625.e: With sunstroke, your head often hurts. You may also feel dizzy and sick and have a red, hot head.
101625.m: A headache after a lot of sun can be sunstroke.

101626.q: What do you do first if someone has sunstroke?
a: Carry on playing in the sun
101626.e: The person must get out of the sun at once. In the shade, the head can recover.
101626.m: With sunstroke, go into the shade at once.

101627.q: What do you cool the head with if someone has sunstroke?
101627.e: Cool, wet cloths on the head and neck help. They take away heat.
101627.m: Cool cloths help a hot head.

101628.q: How does the head often feel with sunstroke?
101628.e: With sunstroke, the head is usually hot and red. The rest of the body, however, can be normally warm.
101628.m: A hot, red head fits with sunstroke.

101629.e: A hat or cap keeps the sun off your head. That way the brain does not overheat.
101629.m: A hat is the best protection against sunstroke.

101630.q: How should a person with sunstroke lie?
a: On their tummy in the sun
101630.e: You raise the upper body and head a little. That takes pressure off the head.
101630.m: With sunstroke, the head lies a little higher.

101631.q: What should someone with sunstroke drink?
101631.e: If the person is conscious, they may drink water in sips. That replaces the fluid they have lost.
101631.m: After a lot of sun, drink water in small sips.

a: The whole body gets too hot
101632.e: With heatstroke, the body can no longer get rid of its heat. The body temperature rises dangerously high.
101632.m: Heatstroke means the whole body overheats.

101633.e: Heatstroke can be life-threatening. You must get help immediately.

101634.q: Where must you never leave children and animals alone in summer?
a: In the garden in the shade
At the swimming pool with supervision
101634.e: A car in the sun gets very hot inside very quickly. That can lead to heatstroke.
101634.m: In summer, nobody stays alone in a parked car.

101635.q: What helps against heatstroke on hot days?
101635.e: If you drink enough, you can sweat and cool your body that way. That helps prevent heatstroke.
101635.m: On hot days, drink lots of water.

101636.q: When should you not do tiring sport on hot days?
a: At midday and in the afternoon
101636.e: It is hottest at midday and in the afternoon. Sport is better early in the morning or in the evening.
101636.m: In summer, it is better to do sport in the morning or evening.

101637.q: How high can body temperature rise with heatstroke?
101637.e: Normal is about 37 degrees Celsius. With heatstroke, the temperature often rises above 40 degrees.
101637.m: A body temperature over 40 degrees is dangerous.

101638.q: How do you cool someone with heatstroke until help arrives?
101638.e: You take the person to a cool place and cool them with damp cloths. At the same time, you call the emergency number.
101638.m: When overheated, the body needs shade and cooling.

101639.e: An object blocks the light. Behind it, there is a darker area: the shadow.
101639.m: A shadow forms where something blocks the light.

101640.e: At midday, the sun is highest. The light falls steeply from above, and the shadow is short.
101640.m: Your shadow is shortest at midday.

101641.q: Your shadow is shorter than you. What does that mean?
a: The sun is strong, protect yourself
101641.e: If your shadow is shorter than you, the sun is high. Then UV radiation is strong.
101641.m: If your shadow is short, you need sun protection.

101642.q: Why is it cooler in the shade?
a: The sun does not shine directly there
101642.e: In the shade, the warm rays of the sun do not hit us directly. That is why it is more pleasant there.
101642.m: In the shade, the sun does not warm you directly.

101643.q: What is a large umbrella that gives shade called?
101643.e: A parasol keeps off the sun's rays. Underneath it is shady and cooler.

101644.q: Does shade protect you completely from UV rays?
101644.e: Some UV radiation reaches you even in the shade, for example from the sky and from bright surfaces. That is why you still need sun cream.
101644.m: Even in the shade, you need some sun protection.

a: In the morning and in the evening
101645.e: In the morning and evening, the sun is low. The light comes in at a flat angle and makes long shadows.
101645.m: A low sun makes long shadows.

101646.q: What does the abbreviation SPF on sun cream stand for?
101646.e: SPF stands for sun protection factor. It shows how strongly the cream protects against sunburn.
101646.m: The sun protection factor shows how strong the sun cream is.

101647.q: Which sun protection factor protects most strongly?
101647.e: The higher the number, the stronger the protection. SPF 50 protects more than SPF 30 or 15.
101647.m: The higher the sun protection factor, the stronger the protection.

101648.q: What must you do with sun cream after swimming?
a: Let it dry and leave it
101648.e: Water and drying yourself rub some of the cream off. That is why you put more on afterwards.
101648.m: After swimming, put on more sun cream.

101649.q: When is the best time to put on sun cream?
a: Before going out in the sun
Only once your skin is red
101649.e: The cream should already be working when the sun hits your skin. That is why you put it on before going out.
101649.m: Sun cream goes on before you go outside.

101650.q: Which places do people often forget when putting on sun cream?
a: The soles of the feet inside shoes
101650.e: Ears, neck and nose get lots of sun. But they are easy to forget when putting on cream.
101650.m: Your ears and neck need sun cream too.

101651.q: How much sun cream should you use?
101651.e: With too little cream, the sun protection factor does not work properly. You should apply it generously.
101651.m: Sun cream must be applied generously.

101652.q: Does sun cream protect you all day without a break?
a: No, you have to put more on
101652.e: Sweat, water and rubbing remove the cream. That is why you have to put more on during the day.
101652.m: You have to reapply sun cream during the day.

101653.q: What sun protection factor do children need at least?
a: A high one, about 30 or more
101653.e: Children's skin is sensitive and burns quickly. That is why a high sun protection factor is recommended.
101653.m: Children's skin needs a high sun protection factor.

101654.q: What does the UV index show?
a: How strong the UV radiation is
101654.e: The UV index is a number for the strength of UV radiation. The higher the number, the faster you get sunburnt.
101654.m: The UV index measures the strength of UV radiation.

101655.q: What does a high UV index mean?
101655.e: With a high UV index, skin gets sunburnt quickly. Then you need a hat, clothes and sun cream.
101655.m: A high UV index means lots of sun protection.

101656.q: From which UV index should you protect yourself?
101656.e: Sun protection is recommended from a UV index of 3. Below 3, the radiation is low.
101656.m: From UV index 3, you need sun protection.

101657.q: What is best at midday when the UV index is high?
a: Lying in the sun for a long time
101657.e: UV radiation is strongest at midday. When the UV index is high, you look for shade at this time.
101657.m: When the UV index is high, stay in the shade at midday.

101658.q: At what time of day is the UV index usually highest?
a: Late at 9 o'clock in the evening
101658.e: At midday, the sun is highest. Then UV radiation is strongest.
101658.m: The UV index is highest around midday.

101659.q: In which season is the UV index in the lowlands usually highest?
101659.e: In summer, the sun is very high at midday. That is why UV radiation is strongest then.
101659.m: UV radiation is strongest in summer.

101660.q: What does a UV index of 11 or more mean?
101660.e: Values of 11 and above count as extreme. Unprotected skin then burns very quickly.
101660.m: A UV index of 11 or more is extreme.

101661.q: Where can you find tomorrow's UV index?
101661.e: Many weather forecasts and weather apps show the UV index. That way you can be prepared.
101661.m: The weather forecast often shows the UV index too.

101662.q: How does a dog, which hardly sweats, cool down?
a: It pants with its mouth open
101662.e: Dogs only have a few sweat glands, mainly on their paws. They cool down mainly by panting.

101663.q: Which clothes feel comfortable when you sweat in summer?
a: Several jackets on top of each other
101663.e: Airy clothes let sweat evaporate. That way the body can cool itself better.
101663.m: In summer, wear light, airy clothes.

101664.e: Chilblains are red or bluish swellings of the skin. They often itch or burn.
101664.m: A chilblain is an itchy swelling caused by cold.

101665.e: Chilblains form mainly on fingers, toes and sometimes the ears. These places cool down quickly.
101665.m: Chilblains often appear on fingers and toes.

101666.q: Which weather makes chilblains more likely?
101666.e: Chilblains form in damp cold, even when it is not below zero. Wet socks are a typical cause.

101667.q: How does a chilblain often feel?
a: It is ice cold and hard as glass
101667.e: Chilblains often itch and burn, especially when you come back into the warm. That is unpleasant.

101668.q: What protects your feet from chilblains?
101668.e: Dry, warm socks keep your feet warm. Wet socks chill the skin.
101668.m: Dry, warm socks protect your feet.

101669.q: Are chilblains the same as frostbite?
a: No, the skin is not frozen
101669.e: With chilblains, the skin is not frozen but irritated by damp cold. With frostbite, on the other hand, tissue freezes.

101670.q: What do you do if you have been playing in the snow with wet gloves?
a: Carry on playing with wet ones
Put your hands in the snow
Put the gloves on the ice
101670.e: Wet gloves chill your hands quickly. Dry gloves keep them warm again.
101670.m: Swap wet gloves for dry ones.

101671.q: What colour is the skin often with a chilblain?
101671.e: Chilblains are usually red or bluish. The area is often swollen too.

101672.e: In great cold, tissue can freeze. That damages the skin and the parts underneath.

101673.q: Which parts of the body are most likely to get frostbite?
101673.e: Fingers, toes, nose and ears are far from the inside of the body. They cool down fastest.
101673.m: Fingers, toes, nose and ears get frostbite first.

101674.q: What does frostbitten skin often look like?
101674.e: Frostbitten skin is often white, grey or waxy. It feels hard and cold.
101674.m: Frostbitten skin is often white and hard.

101675.q: What do you often feel in a frostbitten spot?
101675.e: Because of the cold, the nerves work badly. The spot feels numb.

101676.q: Should you rub frostbitten skin with snow?
101676.e: Rubbing with snow injures the skin even more and cools it further. That is an old mistake.
101676.m: Never rub frostbitten skin with snow.

101677.q: What is the right way to warm a frostbitten spot?
a: Slowly, for example with body heat
101677.e: You warm it gently, for example in the armpit or with lukewarm water. Too much heat harms the skin.

101678.q: Why does cold feel stronger when it is windy?
a: The wind takes away more heat
The wind only dries your hair
101678.e: Wind blows away the warm air right next to the skin. That way the body cools down faster.

101679.q: What protects your fingers from frostbite in winter?
101679.e: Gloves keep the warmth on your hands. Mittens are especially warm.

101680.q: Why do your teeth chatter when you are cold?
101680.e: When we are cold, our muscles shiver very fast. The jaw muscles shiver too, so the teeth chatter.
101680.m: Chattering teeth come from shivering muscles.

101681.q: What is shivering from cold for?
101681.e: Working muscles produce heat. Shivering helps the body to warm up.

101682.q: Which muscles move when your teeth chatter?
101682.e: The jaw muscles open and close the mouth. When they shiver, the teeth knock together.
101682.m: When your teeth chatter, your jaw muscles are shivering.

101683.q: What often appears on the skin at the same time as chattering teeth?
101683.e: When it is cold, the tiny hairs stand up. The skin gets little bumps: goose bumps.
101683.m: When it is cold, you often get goose bumps.

101684.q: What helps when your teeth are chattering with cold?
101684.e: Warm clothes keep heat in the body. Moving about produces extra heat.
101684.m: Warm clothes and moving about help against feeling cold.

101685.q: Can you simply stop shivering from cold on purpose?
101685.e: The body controls shivering by itself. You can hardly stop it by choice.
101685.m: Shivering from cold happens all by itself.

101686.q: When do your teeth often chatter after swimming?
a: When you stand wet in the wind
When you lie in the sun
When you have had a warm shower
101686.e: Wet skin loses a lot of heat through evaporation and wind. Then you quickly get cold.

101687.q: What do chattering teeth tell you?
101687.e: Chattering teeth are a sign that the body is losing too much heat. You should then warm up.
101687.m: Chattering teeth mean your body is cold.

101688.q: What did the Inuit make their snow goggles from in the past?
101688.e: The Inuit carved goggles from wood, bone or antler. Narrow slits let only a little light through.
101688.m: The Inuit carved snow goggles from wood and bone.

101689.q: What did old Inuit snow goggles have instead of lenses?
101689.e: Only a little light gets into the eye through a narrow slit. Even so, people could still see well.
101689.m: Narrow slits let only a little light into the eye.

101690.q: Do you need protective goggles in the snow even when it is cloudy?
a: Yes, the light is still strong
101690.e: A lot of UV radiation gets through clouds too, and the snow reflects it. That is why protection is important even when it is cloudy.
101690.m: Even when it is cloudy, protect your eyes in the snow.

101691.q: What do glacier glasses have at the sides?
101691.e: On glaciers, light comes from all sides. Side shields block this light too.
101691.m: Glacier glasses protect your eyes from the side too.

101692.q: What protects your skin better from UV rays at the beach?
101692.e: Clothes block a large part of the UV rays. Wet skin, on the other hand, does not protect you.
101692.m: Clothes are good protection against UV rays.

101693.q: Who is especially at risk in great heat?
101693.e: Small children and old people are less able to control their body heat. They need extra protection in the heat.
101693.m: Children and old people need special protection in the heat.

101694.q: What is it called when the whole body gets too cold?
101694.e: With hypothermia, the temperature of the whole body drops too far. That is an emergency.
101694.m: When the whole body gets too cold, it is called hypothermia.

101695.q: What helps you sweat less in summer?
101695.e: In the shade, the body heats up less. Then it has less heat to get rid of.
101695.m: You sweat less in the shade.

101696.q: Why do you feel so sticky on muggy days?
a: It is raining on your skin
101696.e: On muggy days, there is already a lot of water in the air. So sweat stays on the skin and does not cool you well.
101696.m: In muggy air, sweat does not cool you well.

101697.q: Which animal sweats a lot when it gallops fast?
101697.e: Horses have many sweat glands in their skin. After running fast, you often see wet fur and white foam.
101697.m: Horses sweat a lot when they work hard.

101698.q: What do many people use against the smell of sweat under the arms?
101698.e: A deodorant reduces the smell under the arms. You put it on clean skin.
101698.m: A deodorant helps against the smell of sweat.

101699.q: What do you do if a friend suddenly becomes confused in the heat and falls over?
a: Get adults and help at once
Go into the sun with them
101699.e: Confusion and passing out in the heat can be signs of heatstroke. Then help is needed at once.
101699.m: In an emergency, get help at once.

101700.q: Why should ski goggles fit tightly against your face?
a: So no wind or snow gets in
So they do not steam up
101700.e: Goggles that fit tightly keep the wind and snowflakes away from your eyes. That way your eyes do not water.
101700.m: Ski goggles fit closely against your face.

101701.q: When do your eyes usually start to hurt after too much sun in the snow?
101701.e: You often only feel the damage from UV rays after a few hours. But by then it is already too late.
101701.m: You often only feel eye damage from the sun later.

101702.q: How does a hat with a wide brim help you in bright light?
101702.e: The brim keeps light from above away from your eyes. That way you need to squint less.
101702.m: A wide hat brim protects against glare.

101703.q: Can you see a clear shadow on a very cloudy day?
101703.e: Clouds spread the light in all directions. That is why there are almost no sharp shadows.
101703.m: With thick clouds, there are hardly any shadows.

101704.q: Should you scratch an itchy chilblain?
101704.e: Scratching can break the delicate skin and make it inflamed. It is better to keep the spot warm and protected.
101704.m: It is better not to scratch chilblains.

101705.q: What is the strong shivering called when a fever is rising?
101705.e: When a fever rises, you feel cold and shiver hard. Your teeth may chatter too.
101705.m: With the chills, you shiver hard even though you have a fever.

101706.q: Why do ski goggles sometimes steam up on the inside?
a: Warm, damp air cools on the lens
101706.e: The air from your face is warm and damp. On the cold lens, it turns into a thin film of water.
101706.m: Warm breath makes cold glass steam up.

101990.q: What do you call relaxed, easy running as a sport?
101990.e: When you jog, you run easily and not very fast. That way you can run for a long time.

101991.q: Which shoes are best to wear for jogging?
101991.e: Running shoes are light and cushion every step. That protects your feet and knees.
101991.m: For jogging, wear good running shoes.

101992.q: How can you tell that you are not running too fast when jogging?
101992.e: If you can still chat while jogging, you are running at the right speed. That way you can keep going for a long time.
101992.m: When jogging, you should still be able to talk.

101993.q: Which surface is especially gentle on your joints when jogging?
101993.e: A woodland path cushions your steps a little. That is gentle on your feet, knees and joints.
101993.m: Jogging on soft woodland paths is gentle on your joints.

101994.q: What is a running race of about 42 kilometres called?
101994.e: A marathon is exactly 42.195 kilometres long. In Switzerland, for example, there are marathons in Zurich and Lucerne.
101994.m: A marathon is about 42 kilometres long.

101995.q: What is a running trail in the woods with exercise stations called in Switzerland?
101995.e: On the Vitaparcours, you jog through the woods. At the stations, you do exercises such as jumping or pull-ups.
101995.m: On the Vitaparcours, you jog and exercise in the woods.

101996.q: Roughly how many kilometres long is a half marathon?
101996.e: A half marathon is exactly 21.0975 kilometres long. That is half the marathon distance.
101996.m: A half marathon is about 21 kilometres long.

101997.q: What do you wear when you go jogging at dusk?
101997.e: A high-visibility vest shines brightly in car headlights. That way you can be seen from far away.
101997.m: In the dark, a high-visibility vest makes you visible.

101998.q: What do you wear on your head for protection when cycling?
101998.e: A bike helmet protects your head if you fall. It must fit well and be fastened firmly.
101998.m: When cycling, a helmet protects your head.

101999.q: What do you use to brake on a bike?
101999.e: The brake levers are on the handlebars. When you pull them, the wheels slow down.
101999.m: On a bike, you brake with the brake levers.

102000.q: What do you signal with your outstretched arm when cycling?
102000.e: With your arm stretched out, you show which way you are turning. That way others know what you are about to do.
102000.m: Before turning, you stretch out your arm.

102001.q: Which test for road safety do many Swiss schoolchildren take?
102001.e: In many cantons, children take the cycling test at primary school. They show that they know the rules of the road.
102001.m: Through the cycling test, children learn the rules of the road.

102002.q: What must light up on a bike when it is dark?
102002.e: A white light shines at the front and a red light at the back. That way everyone else in traffic can see you.
102002.m: In the dark, a bike needs lights at the front and back.

102003.q: Which parts of the body work hardest when cycling?
102003.e: When you push the pedals, it is mainly the muscles in your legs that work. That makes your legs strong.

102004.q: Which side of the road do you cycle on in Switzerland?
102004.e: In Switzerland, traffic drives on the right. Bikes ride on the right-hand edge of the road.
102004.m: In Switzerland, you ride on the right.

102005.q: What do you use on a bike to make others notice you?
102005.e: You ring the bell so that others can hear you. That is important with pedestrians, for example.
102005.m: You warn others with the bell.

102006.q: In which swimming stroke do you lie on your back?
102006.e: In backstroke, you lie on your back. Your face looks up out of the water.
102006.m: In backstroke, you lie on your back.

102007.q: Which swimming stroke is also named after an insect?
102007.e: The dolphin stroke is also called butterfly. Both arms swing over the water at the same time.

102008.q: Which organisation publishes the well-known water safety rules in Switzerland?
102008.e: The SLRG is the Swiss Lifesaving Society. Its water safety rules help prevent accidents in the water.
102008.m: In Switzerland, the SLRG publishes the water safety rules.

102009.q: What does a water safety rule say about murky, unfamiliar water?
a: Take a run-up and jump in
Jump in with your eyes closed
102009.e: In murky water, you cannot see whether there are stones or branches in it. That is why you should not jump in.
102009.m: Do not jump into unfamiliar water.

102010.q: What helps small children who cannot swim yet in the water?
102010.e: Armbands are filled with air and help children stay afloat. Even so, an adult must always keep watch.
102010.m: Small children need help and supervision in the water.

102011.q: Why do you not run along the edge of the pool at the swimming baths?
102011.e: The floor by the pool is wet and smooth. If you run, you can slip and hurt yourself.
102011.m: Walk slowly on the wet poolside.

102012.q: How long is an Olympic swimming pool?
102012.e: At the Olympic Games, swimmers race in a 50-metre pool. Many indoor pools have shorter 25-metre pools.
102012.m: An Olympic pool is 50 metres long.

102013.q: What is the person who keeps an eye on swimmers at the swimming pool called?
102013.e: The lifeguard makes sure nobody gets into danger. They can help if someone has problems in the water.
102013.m: At the swimming pool, the lifeguard keeps watch.

102014.q: What do you wear around your hips and legs when rope climbing?
102014.e: The rope is knotted onto the climbing harness. The harness holds you if you fall onto the rope.
102014.m: When climbing, you wear a climbing harness.

102015.q: What is climbing without a rope on low walls above thick mats called?
102015.e: When bouldering, you only climb so high that you can jump down onto the mat. That is why you do not need a rope.
102015.m: Bouldering is climbing without a rope at jumping height.

102016.q: What holds you if you slip while climbing on a high wall?
102016.e: The rope is fastened to your harness. It catches you if you slip.
102016.m: When climbing high, the rope holds you.

102017.q: What does the person standing at the bottom holding the rope do when you climb?
102017.e: This person is called the belayer. They hold the rope and brake if you fall.
102017.m: The belayer holds the rope when you climb.

102018.q: Why do climbers rub white powder on their hands?
102018.e: The powder is called chalk (magnesium carbonate). It makes your hands dry, so you slip less.
102018.m: Chalk keeps your hands dry when climbing.

102019.q: In which city was sport climbing part of the Olympic Games for the first time?
102019.e: Sport climbing became an Olympic sport for the first time at the Tokyo Summer Games. The Games took place in 2021.
102019.m: Sport climbing became Olympic in Tokyo.

102020.q: What does a helmet protect you from when climbing on rock?
102020.e: On rock, stones can come loose and fall down. The helmet then protects your head.
102020.m: On rock, a helmet protects you from stones.

102021.e: Climbing shoes fit tightly on your foot. The rubber sole grips well on small footholds.
102021.m: Climbing shoes are tight and have a grippy sole.

102022.q: On which piece of gym equipment do you bounce up on a stretched sheet?
102022.e: A trampoline has a jumping bed that hangs on springs. It throws you upwards.
102022.m: You bounce high on a trampoline.

102023.q: What is the exercise called where you roll forwards over your head?
102023.e: In a forward roll, you curl up round like a ball. Then you roll over your back.
102023.m: In a forward roll, you curl up round.

102024.q: Which piece of gym equipment hangs from the ceiling on two ropes?
102024.e: The rings hang freely from the ceiling. You hold on to them and swing or hang.
102024.m: On the rings, you hang and swing.

102025.q: What do you stand on when you do a handstand?
102025.e: In a handstand, you support yourself on your hands. Your legs point straight up.
102025.m: In a handstand, you stand on your hands.

102026.q: What is put under gym equipment so that you land softly?
102026.e: Gym mats are thick and soft. They protect you when you fall or land.

102027.q: What is the balance beam for?
102027.e: The balance beam is a narrow beam. You practise your balance on it.
102027.m: On the balance beam, you practise balance.

102028.q: What is the big Swiss gymnastics festival that takes place about every six years called?
102028.e: At the Federal Gymnastics Festival, many thousands of gymnasts meet. In 2025 it took place in Lausanne.
102028.m: The Federal Gymnastics Festival is the biggest gymnastics festival in Switzerland.

102029.q: In which exercise do you turn sideways over your hands and feet?
102029.e: In a cartwheel, you put your hands down first and then your feet. You turn to the side like a wheel.
102029.m: In a cartwheel, you turn sideways.

102030.q: In which exercise do you lie on your back and stretch your legs straight up?
102030.e: In the candlestick, you support your back with your hands. Your legs point straight up like a candle.
102030.m: In the candlestick, your legs point upwards.

102031.q: How many players does a football team have on the pitch?
102031.e: A team has eleven players on the pitch. One of them is the goalkeeper.
102031.m: In football, eleven players play per team.

102032.q: Who may catch the ball with their hands in football?
102032.e: Only the goalkeeper may touch the ball with their hands. That only applies inside their penalty area.
102032.m: Only the goalkeeper may use their hands.

102033.q: How long does a normal adult football match last?
102033.e: A match has two halves of 45 minutes each. Together that makes 90 minutes.

102034.q: Which card does the referee show to send a player off?
102034.e: For a serious foul, the referee shows the red card. The player then has to leave the pitch.
102034.m: With a red card, you have to leave the pitch.

102035.q: What does the yellow card mean in football?
102035.e: The yellow card is a caution. Anyone who gets two yellow cards in the same match has to leave the pitch.
102035.m: The yellow card is a caution.

102036.q: What is the Swiss national football team often called for short?
102036.e: The Swiss call their national team “Nati” for short. It plays in red shirts.
102036.m: The Swiss national team is called the Nati for short.

102038.q: In which Swiss city does the world football association FIFA have its headquarters?
102038.e: FIFA has its headquarters in Zurich. It organises the Football World Cup, for example.

102039.q: What is the hopping game with boxes drawn on the ground called?
102039.e: In hopscotch, you hop on one leg through the boxes. First you throw a stone into one of the squares.
102039.m: In hopscotch, you hop through boxes.

102040.q: What do you use to draw game courts on the playground?
102040.e: Pavement chalk is thick and colourful. You can draw on tarmac with it, and the rain washes it away again.
102040.m: You draw on the ground with pavement chalk.

102041.q: What is the game called where everyone hides and one child looks for them?
102041.e: In hide-and-seek, one child counts with their eyes closed. Then they look for the others.
102041.m: In hide-and-seek, one child looks for the others.

102042.q: In which game does a rope swing over your head and under your feet?
102042.e: When skipping, you jump over the rope each time. That trains stamina and skill.
102042.m: When skipping, you jump over the rope.

102043.q: On which piece of playground equipment do you whizz from the top to the bottom sitting down?
102043.e: On the slide, you climb up a ladder. Then you slide down the smooth chute.
102043.m: On the slide, you slide down.

102044.q: In which game do you jump over a stretched elastic band?
102044.e: In French skipping, two children hold the elastic stretched with their legs. A third child jumps in and out following the rules.
102044.m: In French skipping, you jump over an elastic band.

102045.q: On which piece of playground equipment do two children go up and down?
102045.e: On the seesaw, one child sits at each end. In Switzerland, it is often also called “Gigampfi”.
102045.m: On the seesaw, you go up and down.

102046.q: What gets warm and loose when you warm up?
102046.e: Moving makes more blood flow into the muscles. That makes them warm and loose.
102046.m: When you warm up, your muscles get warm.

102047.q: What is a good warm-up exercise?
a: Sitting still for a long time
102047.e: Easy running and hopping slowly get the body going. After that, you can get faster and stronger.
102047.m: To warm up, you first move gently.

102048.q: Roughly how long does a warm-up in school PE last?
102048.e: A warm-up usually lasts about 10 to 15 minutes. That is enough for the body to be ready.
102048.m: A warm-up lasts about ten minutes.

102049.q: What happens to your pulse when you warm up?
102049.e: Your pulse shows how fast your heart is beating. When you warm up, it slowly gets faster.
102049.m: When you warm up, your pulse rises slowly.

102050.q: What do you call slow running after training?
102050.e: When cooling down, the body calms down again. Pulse and breathing slowly become calmer.
102050.m: After sport, you cool down with slow running.

102051.q: In which exercise do you jump and clap your hands together above your head?
102051.e: In star jumps, you jump your legs apart and back together again. At the same time, your arms go up and down.
102051.m: Star jumps are a good warm-up exercise.

102052.q: Which exercise loosens your shoulders when you warm up?
102052.e: In arm circles, your arms turn in big circles. Your shoulder joints move as you do this.

102053.q: Where do PE lessons take place when it rains?
102053.e: The sports hall is a big room for sport. You can do gym and play games there in any weather.
102053.m: When it rains, PE is in the sports hall.

102054.q: At least how many PE lessons per week does the Swiss federal government require for compulsory school (not including kindergarten)?
102054.e: The Swiss Sport Promotion Act requires at least three PE lessons per week. This rule does not apply to kindergarten.
102054.m: In Swiss schools, there are at least three PE lessons per week.

102055.q: Which shoes do you wear in the sports hall?
102055.e: Trainers with light-coloured soles do not leave black marks on the hall floor. They do not slip either.
102055.m: In the sports hall, you wear clean trainers.

102056.q: In which ball game do you throw the ball into a basket?
102056.e: In basketball, the basket hangs high on a board. If you throw the ball in, you score points.
102056.m: In basketball, you shoot at a basket.

102057.q: In which game do you try to hit opponents with a ball?
102057.e: In dodgeball, there are two courts. Anyone hit by the ball has to leave the court.
102057.m: In dodgeball, you hit opponents with the ball.

102058.q: What is the day called when the whole school does competitions outdoors?
102058.e: On sports day, there are races, jumps, throws and games. Often all classes take part.
102058.m: On sports day, all classes do competitions.

102059.q: Where do you land in the long jump?
102059.e: In the long jump, you jump into a pit of sand. The distance is measured to the mark you make.
102059.m: In the long jump, you land in sand.

102060.e: In a sprint, you run as fast as you can. The distance is short, for example 60 or 80 metres.
102060.m: A sprint is a short, fast run.

102061.q: What do you hold in your hands when skiing?
102061.e: Ski poles help with balance and pushing off. You also use them when turning.
102061.m: When skiing, you hold ski poles.

102062.q: What protects your eyes from wind and snow when skiing?
102062.e: Ski goggles fit closely around your eyes. They protect against wind, snow and bright light.

102063.q: What is a ski race called where you ski tightly around lots of gates?
102063.e: In slalom, the gates are close together. You have to make lots of quick turns.
102063.m: In slalom, you ski around lots of gates.

102064.q: How do you get comfortably up the mountain when skiing?
102064.e: Ski lifts and chairlifts pull or carry you uphill. Then you ski down.
102064.m: The ski lift takes you uphill.

102065.q: Which Swiss skier won the overall World Cup in alpine skiing several times in a row from 2022?
102065.e: Marco Odermatt from Nidwalden won the overall World Cup every year from 2022 to 2026, so five times in a row (as of 2026). He is one of the best skiers in the world.
102065.m: Marco Odermatt is a Swiss ski star.

102066.q: How do beginners position their skis to brake?
102066.e: In a snowplough, the ski tips point towards each other and the ends point apart. That slows you down.

102067.q: What colour are the easiest ski runs in Switzerland?
102067.e: In Switzerland, easy runs are blue. Intermediate runs are marked red and difficult ones black.

102068.q: Why do you need sun cream in the snow, even in winter?
a: The sun is bigger in winter
102068.e: Snow strongly reflects sunlight. That is why you quickly get sunburnt in the mountains.
102068.m: In the snow, you need sun protection.

102069.q: Where does the famous Lauberhorn race take place?
102069.e: The Lauberhorn race is one of the longest downhill races in the World Cup. It takes place every January in Wengen in the Bernese Oberland.
102069.m: The Lauberhorn race is in Wengen.

102070.q: What colour are normal hiking signposts in Switzerland?
102070.e: Swiss hiking trails are marked with yellow signposts. They show destinations and times.

102071.q: What colours are the markings of a mountain hiking trail?
102071.e: Mountain hiking trails are marked white-red-white. They are steeper and more difficult than normal hiking trails.
102071.m: Mountain hiking trails are marked white-red-white.

102072.q: Which shoes do you wear when hiking in the mountains?
102072.e: Walking boots have a thick sole with tread. They give good grip on stony paths.
102072.m: In the mountains, you wear walking boots.

102073.q: What is the food you take with you on a hike called?
102073.e: Provisions are food for the journey, for example bread, cheese and fruit. You carry them in your rucksack.
102073.m: Provisions are food for the journey.

102074.q: What does the time on a Swiss hiking signpost show?
a: Roughly how long you will walk
102074.e: The signposts show roughly how many hours and minutes you need to reach the destination. That way you can plan the hike.
102074.m: The signpost shows the approximate walking time.

102075.q: What do you do with your rubbish on a hike?
a: I take it back with me
I throw it in the stream
102075.e: Rubbish harms nature and animals. That is why you pack it up and throw it away at home.
102075.m: Take your rubbish back home with you.

102076.q: Why do you take a jacket on a mountain hike, even on a sunny day?
a: Because the weather in the mountains changes quickly
Because you walk faster in a jacket
Because you have to sit on it
Because otherwise the rucksack is empty
102076.e: In the mountains, it can quickly become cool, windy or rainy. With a jacket, you are prepared for that.
102076.m: In the mountains, the weather changes quickly.

102077.q: What do many families in Switzerland do at a fireplace when hiking?
102077.e: In Switzerland, grilling something over an open fire is called “bräteln”. Cervelat sausages on a stick are popular.
102077.m: On a hike, people like to grill a sausage.

102078.q: What do you carry your drinks and rain jacket in when hiking?
102078.e: A rucksack is carried on your back. That way you have both hands free.
102078.m: When hiking, you carry a rucksack.

102079.q: What does stamina mean in sport?
a: Being able to keep going for a long time
Being able to jump very high
Being able to lift very heavy things
Being able to aim very well
102079.e: If you have stamina, you can keep moving for a long time without getting tired quickly. For example, when running a long way.
102079.m: Stamina means being able to keep going for a long time.

102080.q: Which sport is a typical endurance sport?
102080.e: In cross-country skiing, you move for a long time without a break. You need a lot of stamina for it.
102080.m: Cross-country skiing is an endurance sport.

102081.q: Which organs get stronger through endurance training?
102081.e: If you regularly run, swim or cycle, you train your heart and lungs. They then work better.
102081.m: Endurance training strengthens your heart and lungs.

102082.q: What is the big cycle race through Switzerland that lasts several days called?
102082.e: The Tour de Suisse is a stage race for professional cyclists. The riders need a lot of stamina for it.
102082.m: The Tour de Suisse is a cycle race through Switzerland.

102083.q: Which three sports do you do one after another in a triathlon?
102083.e: In a triathlon, you swim first, then cycle, and finally run. That takes a lot of stamina.
102083.m: A triathlon is made up of swimming, cycling and running.

102084.q: What helps if you get a stitch while running?
102084.e: A stitch is a stabbing pain in your side. If you slow down and breathe calmly, it usually soon goes away.
102084.m: Slowing down helps with a stitch.

102085.q: What is the big cross-country ski race in the Engadine called?
102085.e: Every March, many thousands of people take part in the Engadin Skimarathon on cross-country skis. The course goes from Maloja to S-chanf.
102085.m: The Engadin Skimarathon is a big cross-country ski race.

102086.q: How do you build up more stamina over time?
a: Through sleeping a lot during the day
102086.e: If you train often and regularly, your stamina keeps improving. The body gets used to the effort.
102086.m: You build stamina through regular training.

102351.q: In which unit is a child's height usually given?
102351.e: Height is a length. Lengths are measured in centimetres or metres.

102352.q: At what time of day is a person a tiny bit taller?
102352.e: Lying down at night lets the spine recover. That is why you are about 1 to 2 centimetres taller in the morning than in the evening.
102352.m: You are a little taller in the morning than in the evening.

102353.q: Up to what age do most people grow taller?
102353.e: Most people stop growing taller somewhere between about 16 and 20. After that, their height stays the same for a long time.
102353.m: At about 18 to 20, you have finished growing.

102354.q: Who does a child's height depend on to a large extent?
102354.e: Height is inherited from the parents to a large extent. Tall parents often have tall children.
102354.m: You inherit your height partly from your parents.

102355.q: Lina is 120 cm tall and Tim is 130 cm tall. How many centimetres taller is Tim?
102355.e: You work out 130 minus 120 = 10. So Tim is 10 centimetres taller.
102355.m: You find the difference by subtracting the smaller number.

102356.q: Mia was 115 cm tall. A year later she is 121 cm tall. How much has she grown?
102356.e: You work out 121 minus 115 = 6. Mia has grown 6 centimetres in a year.
102356.m: You work out growth as new height minus old height.

102357.q: What helps a child grow healthily?
102357.e: The body needs building blocks from healthy food to make bones and muscles. Sleep and exercise also help.

102358.q: What do you need a height chart on the wall for?
102358.e: Centimetres are printed on a height chart. You stand in front of it and see how tall you are.
102358.m: You measure your height with a height chart.

102359.q: What is the right way to stand at a height chart?
102359.e: Shoes would make you taller and bent knees shorter. That is why you stand barefoot and straight.
102359.m: At the height chart, you stand barefoot and straight.

102360.q: What do you lay flat on your head when measuring at a height chart?
a: A book or a small board
102360.e: A flat book or board shows exactly where your head ends. That way you can read the number on the wall easily.
102360.m: A flat book on your head helps you read the height.

102361.q: Why do people often write the date next to the line on a height chart?
a: To see when you were that tall
Because otherwise you forget the name
102361.e: With the date, you can compare later. That way you see how much you have grown over a period of time.
102361.m: The date shows when you were how tall.

102362.q: A line on the height chart is at 100 cm. How many metres is that?
102362.e: 100 centimetres is exactly 1 metre. So anyone standing there is 1 metre tall.
102362.m: A line at 100 centimetres means 1 metre.

102363.q: Leo's line was at 110 cm last year. Today it is at 117 cm. How much has Leo grown?
102363.e: You work out 117 minus 110 = 7. Leo has grown 7 centimetres.
102363.m: The gap between two lines shows the growth.

102364.q: How many millimetres are there in one centimetre on the height chart?
102364.e: There are 10 small lines between two centimetre lines. Each of them is a millimetre.

102365.q: How must a height chart hang so that it measures correctly?
a: With the zero at the floor
With the zero at the ceiling
At an angle on the wall
In the middle of the door
102365.e: Height is measured from the floor you are standing on. That is why the start of the height chart must be exactly at the floor.
102365.m: The height chart starts at the floor.

102366.q: What are a child's first teeth called?
102366.e: The first teeth are called milk teeth. They fall out later and are replaced.
102366.m: The first teeth are called milk teeth.

102367.q: Why should you brush milk teeth well, even though they fall out later?
a: They keep space for the new teeth
Otherwise they turn into gold teeth
102367.e: Milk teeth keep the space free for the permanent teeth. Unhealthy milk teeth can also harm the new teeth.
102367.m: Healthy milk teeth are important for the new teeth.

102368.q: What do you call the set of teeth a child has while they have both milk teeth and permanent teeth?
102368.e: While the teeth are changing, old and new teeth are in the mouth together. This set of teeth is called mixed dentition.
102368.m: While your teeth are changing, you have mixed dentition.

102369.q: At about what age does most children's first milk tooth fall out?
102369.e: The change of teeth usually starts at about 6. For some children a little earlier, for others a little later.
102369.m: At about 6, your teeth start to change.

102370.q: What do you call a loose milk tooth just before it falls out?
102370.e: When the new tooth pushes from below, the milk tooth becomes loose and wobbles. It is called a wobbly tooth.
102370.m: A loose milk tooth is called a wobbly tooth.

102371.q: What pushes a milk tooth out when your teeth change?
102371.e: The permanent tooth grows under the milk tooth. It pushes upwards until the milk tooth becomes loose.
102371.m: The new tooth pushes the milk tooth out.

102372.q: What do you call the new teeth that come after the milk teeth?
102372.e: The new teeth are called permanent teeth. They only grow once and have to last a lifetime.
102372.m: After the milk teeth come the permanent teeth.

102373.q: Which made-up character collects the milk tooth that has fallen out in many stories?
102373.e: In many families, the milk tooth is put under the pillow. The tooth fairy brings a little surprise in return.
102373.m: The tooth fairy collects milk teeth.

102374.q: Which teeth appear right at the back at about age 6 without a milk tooth falling out?
102374.e: At about 6, the first permanent molars grow behind the milk teeth. That is why they are also called six-year molars.
102374.m: At about 6, the first big molars come through at the back.

102375.e: Shoe size depends on the length of your foot. The longer your foot, the bigger the number.
102375.m: Shoe size depends on the length of your foot.

102376.q: Why do children often need new shoes?
102376.e: Children's feet grow quickly. That is why their shoes soon get too small and they need bigger ones.
102376.m: Because your feet grow, you need new shoes.

102377.q: How much space should there be at the front of a shoe in front of your toes?
102377.e: When you walk, your foot slides forward a little in the shoe. That is why you need about a thumb's width of space at the front.
102377.m: There should be about a thumb's width of space at the front of the shoe.

102378.q: Which shoe size is most likely to fit a kindergarten child?
102378.e: Children of kindergarten age often wear shoe sizes around 26 to 30 (European sizes). Sizes over 40 are mostly worn by adults.
102378.m: Small children have small shoe sizes.

102379.q: How can you tell that a shoe is too small?
102379.e: If your toes touch the front, your foot has too little room. Then the shoe pinches and can hurt.
102379.m: If your toes touch the front, the shoe is too small.

102380.q: Lars wears shoe size 30. His foot has grown. Which size comes next?
102380.e: Shoe sizes go up in steps of one. After 30 comes 31.

102381.q: At what time of day is it best to try on new shoes?
a: In the middle of the night
102381.e: During the day, your feet swell a little from standing and walking. Shoes that fit in the afternoon will not pinch later.
102381.m: It is best to try on shoes in the afternoon.

102382.q: Are your left and right feet always exactly the same length?
a: No, one is often a bit longer
No, the left one is twice as long
102382.e: In many people, one foot is a tiny bit longer. You buy shoes to fit the longer foot.
102382.m: One foot is often a little longer than the other.

102383.q: Roughly how long is a newborn baby?
102383.e: Most babies are about 48 to 54 centimetres long at birth. That is roughly half a metre.
102383.m: A newborn baby is about 50 centimetres long.

102384.q: Roughly how much does a newborn baby weigh?
102384.e: Most babies weigh between about 3 and 4 kilograms at birth. That is as heavy as a few cartons of milk.
102384.m: A newborn baby weighs about 3.5 kilograms.

102385.q: What does a newborn baby drink?
102385.e: A newborn baby gets breast milk or formula milk from a bottle. It contains everything the baby needs to grow.

102386.q: How does a baby usually show that it is hungry?
102386.e: A baby cannot talk yet. It cries to show that it needs something.
102386.m: A baby cries when it is hungry.

102387.q: At about how many months do many babies get their first tooth?
102387.e: The first milk tooth usually comes at about six months. In some babies earlier, in others later.
102387.m: The first tooth often comes at about 6 months.

102388.q: What does a baby wear because it cannot use the toilet yet?
102388.e: A baby cannot control its bladder yet. The nappy soaks everything up.

102389.q: What else is a baby in its first year called?
102389.e: A baby in its first year is called an infant. It feeds at the breast or from a bottle.
102389.m: A baby in its first year is called an infant.

102390.q: Does a baby have fewer or more bones at birth than an adult?
102390.e: A baby has around 300 bones and parts of bones. Many of them later grow together.
102390.m: A baby has more bones than an adult.

102391.q: Roughly how old is a toddler?
102391.e: After its first birthday, a child is no longer an infant. Until about 3, it is called a toddler.
102391.m: A toddler is about 1 to 3 years old.

102392.q: At about what age do many children take their first steps?
102392.e: Most children learn to walk around their first birthday. Some a little earlier, others later.
102392.m: At about 1, many children learn to walk.

102393.q: Which word do many toddlers say as one of their first?
102393.e: Short words with repeated syllables like “Mama” or “Papa” are easy to say. That is why they are often among the first words.
102393.m: Mama is often one of the first words.

102394.q: At about what age do most children no longer need a nappy during the day?
102394.e: Most children learn to use the potty or toilet between the ages of 2 and 4.
102394.m: At about 3, many children are dry during the day.

102395.q: What is a place called where toddlers are looked after while their parents work?
102395.e: In Switzerland, a nursery is called a Kita, short for Kindertagesstätte. Small children play and eat there while their parents work.
102395.m: Small children are looked after at nursery.

102396.q: At about what age does a child have all its milk teeth?
102396.e: Milk teeth come through one by one. By about two and a half to three, they are usually all there.
102396.m: By about 3, all the milk teeth are there.

102397.e: First you are a baby, then a toddler. At about 6, you become a schoolchild.
102397.m: After the baby comes the toddler, and then the schoolchild.

102398.q: Why must you keep an especially close eye on toddlers?
a: They do not know about many dangers yet
102398.e: Toddlers are curious and do not yet know what is hot, sharp or dangerous. That is why they need protecting.
102398.m: Toddlers do not know about many dangers yet.

102399.q: At what age do you legally become an adult in Switzerland?
102399.e: In Switzerland, you become an adult at 18. Then you can decide many things for yourself.
102399.m: In Switzerland, you become an adult at 18.

102400.q: From what age can you vote in federal votes in Switzerland?
102400.e: Anyone who has Swiss citizenship and is 18 years old may take part in federal votes.
102400.m: At 18, you can vote in Switzerland.

102401.q: What hair grows on the face of many adult men?
102401.e: In many men, hair grows on the chin and cheeks from their teenage years. This hair is called a beard.
102401.m: Many adult men have a beard.

102402.q: Roughly how tall is an adult man in Switzerland on average?
102402.e: Men in Switzerland are on average about 1.78 metres tall. Of course, some are taller and some shorter.
102402.m: A Swiss man is on average about 1.78 metres tall.

102403.q: From what age can you get a learner's permit for a car in Switzerland?
102403.e: Since 2021, you can get a learner's permit for a car in Switzerland at 17. You can take the test at 18 at the earliest.
102403.m: In Switzerland, you can learn to drive from 17.

102404.q: Roughly how many hours of sleep do adults need per night?
102404.e: Adults usually need about 7 to 9 hours of sleep. Children need more.
102404.m: Adults need about 7 to 9 hours of sleep.

102405.q: What do you call someone who is between a child and an adult?
102405.e: Between about 12 and 18, you are a young person. After that, you are an adult.
102405.m: Before becoming an adult, you are a young person.

102406.q: Who needs more sleep per night: a schoolchild or an adult?
102406.e: Children grow and learn a great deal. That is why they need more sleep than adults.
102406.m: Children need more sleep than adults.

102407.q: What else are older people called?
102407.e: Older people are called senior citizens. The word “senior” comes from Latin and means “the older one”.
102407.m: Older people are called senior citizens.

102408.q: What is the pension that older people in Switzerland get from the state called?
102408.e: AHV stands for the Swiss old-age and survivors' insurance. It pays older people in Switzerland a pension every month.
102408.m: In Switzerland, older people get an AHV pension.

102409.q: At what age do men in Switzerland normally retire (as of 2025)?
102409.e: The retirement age in Switzerland is 65 for men. For women, it is also rising to 65 by 2028.
102409.m: In Switzerland, the retirement age is 65.

102410.q: Why do many old people get a little shorter again?
a: The spine sinks down a little
102410.e: In old age, the cushions between the vertebrae get flatter. That is why you get a few centimetres shorter.
102410.m: In old age, people often get a little shorter.

102411.q: What colour does hair often turn in old age?
102411.e: In old age, hair makes less pigment. That is why it turns grey or white.
102411.m: In old age, hair often turns grey.

102412.q: What helps many older people to read small letters?
102412.e: In old age, many people see less well close up. Reading glasses make the writing sharp again.

102413.q: What appears on the skin in old age?
102413.e: With age, skin becomes thinner and less stretchy. That is why wrinkles form.
102413.m: In old age, the skin gets wrinkles.

102414.q: Roughly how old do people in Switzerland live to on average (as of 2024)?
102414.e: Women in Switzerland live to over 85 on average, men to over 82. That is among the highest in the world.
102414.m: In Switzerland, people live to over 80 on average.

102415.q: Which walking aid with wheels and handles helps many older people to walk?
102415.e: A rollator has wheels, handles and brakes. You lean on it and walk more safely.
102415.m: A rollator helps you walk safely.

102416.q: Where do children usually feel growing pains?
102416.e: Growing pains usually occur in the legs, for example in the calves, thighs or the backs of the knees.
102416.m: Growing pains are usually felt in the legs.

102417.q: When do growing pains usually happen?
a: In the evening or at night
102417.e: It is typical for the pain to come in the evening or at night. Sometimes a child wakes up because of it.
102417.m: Growing pains usually come in the evening or at night.

102418.e: Growing pains occur in children. They are not known in babies or older people.

102419.q: What often helps against growing pains?
102419.e: Gentle massage and warmth, for example a warm cushion, soothe the legs. Often a bit of comfort helps too.
102419.m: Gentle massage often helps with growing pains.

a: Yes, you have to go to hospital
Yes, you may never run again
102420.e: Growing pains are unpleasant but usually harmless. They stop by themselves.

102421.q: At what age do children often have growing pains?
102421.e: Growing pains occur mainly in children between about 3 and 12.
102421.m: Growing pains often occur between 3 and 12.

102422.q: When should you go to the doctor with leg pain?
a: If there is swelling or a fever
102422.e: If the leg is swollen or red, or the child has a fever, it is probably not growing pains. Then a doctor should take a look.
102422.m: With swelling or a fever, you go to the doctor.

102423.q: Do we know for certain that growing pains come from growing?
a: No, the cause is not completely clear
102423.e: Despite their name, it has not been proven that they come from growing. Perhaps the muscles are tired from playing during the day.
102423.m: The cause of growing pains is not completely clear.

102424.q: In which unit is body weight given?
102424.e: Weight is measured in kilograms, kg for short. Metres are for lengths, litres for liquids.
102424.m: Body weight is given in kilograms.

102425.q: Roughly how much heavier is a child at 1 year than at birth?
102425.e: A child grows very fast in its first year. At one year, it weighs about three times as much as at birth.
102425.m: At one year, a child is about three times as heavy as at birth.

102426.q: What makes up most of your body weight?
102426.e: About 60 out of every 100 parts of the human body are water. In children, it is even a little more.
102426.m: The body is mostly made of water.

102427.q: Tim weighs 30 kg and his father 80 kg. How much heavier is his father?
102427.e: You work out 80 minus 30 = 50. His father is 50 kilograms heavier.
102427.m: You find the difference in weight by subtracting.

102428.q: Roughly how much does an eight-year-old child weigh?
